```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(fivethirtyeight)
candy <- fivethirtyeight::candy_rankings

most_sugar <- candy |> 
  arrange(desc(sugarpercent)) |> 
  slice(1)

least_sugar <- candy |> 
  arrange(sugarpercent) |> 
  slice(1)

#install.packages("bslib")
#install.packages("bsicons")
library(bslib)
library(bsicons)
#install.packages("shiny")
```

## Most and Least Sugary Candy

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Most Sugary Candy"
#This way was not loading on my website, only showing the code so I co coded with AI

 # icon = "droplet-fill",
  #color = "danger",
  #value = most_sugar$competitorname)
bslib::value_box(
  title = "Most Sugary Candy",
  value = most_sugar$competitorname,
  showcase = bsicons::bs_icon("droplet-fill"),
  theme = "danger"
)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
  theme = "success"
)
```

## How Often Is Sugary Candy Picked?

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
p <- ggplot(candy,aes(x = sugarpercent,y = winpercent)) +
  geom_point(
    aes(text = paste(
      "Candy:", competitorname,
      "<br>Sugar:", round(sugarpercent, 2),
      "<br>Win %:", round(winpercent, 1), "%")), 
    color = "purple",
    size = 3,
    alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_smooth(
    method="lm"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Sugar Rush!",
    subtitle = "Does More Sugar Mean More Popular?",
    x = "Sugar Percentage",
    y = "Win Percentage") +
  theme_minimal()
```
